host.cpu: AMD Ryzen 5 PRO 3400GE w/ Radeon Vega Graphics

nativeAdapter.renderer: AMD Radeon Vega 11 Graphics (radeonsi, raven, ACO, DRM 3.64, 7.0.0-31-generic)

method.memory: Linux proportional set size, entire Chromium tree versus native Blender tree; 200ms sampling
method.timers: Python perf_counter for both builds; render_pre to render_post for both renderers
limitations: Native uses background mode; browser includes its UI, GPU process and JavaScript workers. Baseline and incremental memory are reported separately.
Mesh timings cover CPU construction and evaluation, not interactive viewport frame rate.
Each case runs three times in one process, in fixed order. First and warm timings are included; these are small local baselines, not a broad production-scene benchmark.
Both use the same pinned Blender release and scene settings. Native CPU ISA/accelerators and the Wasm build differ.
First-run means the first render in that process. Global GPU driver caches are not cleared. Native Eevee and browser WebGPU use different graphics APIs on the same hardware.
Physical memory sampling has overhead and may miss sub-200ms peaks. Wasm capacity is not physical usage, and its linear memory cannot shrink after growth.
PSS does not fully account for driver-managed GPU memory; the scene-size test measures CPU geometry memory, not total VRAM.
The 4 GiB Wasm32 limit is configured for this build. Larger desktop-scale allocations have not been ported or validated.

renderOptimization.method: Three fresh Chromium sessions per build, alternated control/candidate. Three renders per session, no video/tracing, original factory settings. First-in-process engine handler time; global GPU driver caches are not cleared.

cyclesReference.reference: Desktop Blender CPU render, factory startup scene with the recorded resolution and sample settings

limitations: Cycles CPU acceptance uses the factory cube at 128x128 and 16 samples, with denoising and adaptive sampling disabled.
Cycles GPU, denoising, progressive display and rendered viewport are not supported.
Final rendering requires the JSPI bundle in current desktop Chromium.
Production Blender uses wasm32 with a 4 GiB linear-memory ceiling. The memory64 result is a separate sparse-addressing probe, not Blender scene-capacity evidence.
NumPy has no BLAS; native subprocesses, arbitrary dynamic extension modules and the extension marketplace remain unsupported.
Device file selection, browser downloads, additional windows and remaining dependency groups are still pending.
Ocean acceptance uses resolution 5 and 12 animation frames. Ocean disk-cache baking is not covered.

OpenVDB acceptance covers float sphere grids, ZIP/Blosc IO, NanoVDB conversion and mesh/volume modifiers. Mantaflow acceptance covers four resolution-16 gas frames; liquid simulation, long bakes and the Python OpenVDB module are not covered.
Alembic acceptance covers Ogawa mesh deformation, UVs and animated transforms; HDF5 archives and other schema types are not covered.
Functional checks ran with other host activity and are not an isolated performance benchmark.
